To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the radiative correction to the neutral current processes is positive (enhancement) and is of the order of 2% if the Higgs mass is 1.5mZ, and that the constant term is negative (decrease) and is of about 1.2% if the same Higgs mass is assumed.

(1) the radiative corrections in the neutral current processes are positive, and (2) the radiative correction to gA, which was thought to be zero, is actually nonzero and negative, and (3) the radiative contribution to the constant term in the neutral current is negative, and (4) the constant term in charged current processes is nonzero and negative.

the radiative correction to the constant term of the charged current induced reactions are −2.0 (−2.2) per cent, if the Hoss boson mass is 1.5mZ(5.0mZ), and the constant term of neutrino‐deuterons reactions induced by the neutral currents is 1.7 per cent, if mH = 5mZ, and 1.5 per cent if mH = mZ.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the radiative correction to the axial vector coupling constant gA is 0.9 (0.8) per cent for the Higgs mass of 1.5 (5.0) mZ.
the one‐loop radiative corrections to low energy neutrino‐deutron reactions are 1.5 (1.2) per cent larger than those given by Kurylow et al.
the radiative correction to the neutral current processes are not negligible and the corrections to the axial‐vector current induced reactions are much more important than previously thought.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the constant term in the radiative corrections is very sensitive to the treatment of the axial‐ vector coupling constant gA.

the constant term is important for the neutral current induced neutrino‐deuterium reactions, and the radiative corrections should be calculated in the same way for both the neutral and charged current induced processes.

the radiative effects in the neutral current induced processes are significantly larger than the corresponding effects in the charged current reactions, and that the latter are not necessarily negligible.
